spec.inputs: Collect these before anything else; ask for whatever is missing, offer the default in brackets. - Product and URL: [name] ([url]) - 8 to 12 UI states that tell the product's story, in order: [state 1 ... state N] - The real data each state shows (labels, numbers, names; no placeholders): [per state] - Brand: colors [bg / ink / one accent], display face [family], UI face [family] - Music: a royalty-free track whose license allows this use, near 120 BPM [or: synthesize a minimal UI score at 120 BPM] - Formats: [9x16 first, then 1x1 and 16x9] - Loop: [yes: the last state morphs back into the first]
spec.direction: A product film made of one shape. The same container is every state: it changes width, height, corner radius and fill from one state to the next and never cuts away. Content inside it swaps behind a short, quick fade while the container moves. A cursor causes every change with a real click, a typed field or a drag. The camera pushes in on small states and pulls back for big ones so each state fills a similar part of the frame. Look: [canvas color], one accent, the product's own type. Springs with at most a hint of overshoot on UI, none on type. Do not use: bouncy easing, glows, gradients on UI chrome, particle bursts, template-looking filler, a beat where nothing happens.
spec.structure: [BPM] BPM, [N] bars, one state per downbeat, something moving on every beat. [state 1] -> [state 2] -> ... -> [state N] -> back to [state 1] Show this as a table: state, bar.beat, start second, what the cursor does, the data on screen, the sounds. The seam from the last state to the first lands on a downbeat like every other change.
spec.build: 1. Route A in the motion-studio project: film/film.js with defineFilm; one scene per state, all drawing the same container; every value computed from t, no CSS transitions, no timers, no state kept between frames. 2. Every property of the container (x, y, w, h, radius, each color channel) is a spring track over the state list: one spring per change, loopTrack() for the loop so frame 0 equals frame duration. 3. Content appears after its container starts morphing and is gone before the next morph: swapAlpha(t, stateStart, nextStart). 4. Tab or list indicators stretch: their two edges ride different springs (indicator()). 5. Drags are direct: while the cursor holds, the value follows the cursor; on release it springs from where it was. 6. Beat grid from the track (node tools/beats.mjs), states on grid.bar(n), UI sounds as cues on grid.beat(n) or on measured hits; the track starts on a downbeat. 7. Stills per beat and the critique loop before any final render; 60 fps with 4 subframes of motion blur (studio.json fps and subframes).
spec.gotchas: Never put will-change, or anything that rasterizes, on elements the camera scales: text goes soft. Text that swaps inside a moving container needs its own in and out timing or two labels overlap. The last frame must match the first: container, content, cursor position and cursor speed. A seam change is a key at t = 0 with the pre-seam value as the first key; keys never sit at t = duration. A hard on/off blink (caret, highlight) can register as a single-frame pop; pulse it with a smooth curve.
spec.start: Ask for the inputs first. Then show the state list on the beat grid (the table described in the structure section) and wait for approval before writing any film code. A rejected list is rewritten, not coded around.
